t: A Christian monarchy that united eastern and western Georgia in 1008 under the Bagratid dynasty.
Under David the Builder and Queen Tamar it dominated the Caucasus and enjoyed a golden age of poetry and church building.
Mongol conquest, Timur’s invasions and rebellious regional lords broke it into separate kingdoms by 1490.
dyk: David the Builder settled thousands of Kipchak families from the steppes in Georgia as soldiers, and Tamar was crowned with the title of king rather than queen.
ev: Bagrat III unites western and eastern Georgia
David IV routs a Muslim coalition at the Battle of Didgori
David IV captures Tbilisi and makes it his capital
Georgian-backed Komnenos brothers found the Empire of Trebizond
Queen Rusudan submits to the Mongols
Timur takes Tbilisi and captures King Bagrat V
A royal council accepts the division of Georgia into separate kingdoms

f.predecessor: Kingdom of Abkhazia; Kingdom of the Iberians
f.successor: Kingdom of Kartli; Kingdom of Kakheti; Kingdom of Imereti; Principality of Samtskhe
